title: Tamarind Rice (Puliyodarai)
tagline: Tangy, spicy temple-style rice coated in a rich roasted tamarind paste.
intro: Puliyodarai, or tamarind rice, is a South Indian temple classic prized for its complex sweet-sour-spicy flavour. A special paste (pulikachal) of roasted spices, lentils and tamarind is cooked down, then folded through rice. It keeps well and travels beautifully, which is why it's a favourite prasadam and journey food.
rice: Cooked, cooled short-grain or sona masoori rice

items: Lime-sized ball of tamarind, soaked in 250 ml warm water
1 tbsp chana dal, 1 tbsp urad dal

method: Dry-roast the spice-powder ingredients until fragrant, cool, and grind to a coarse powder.
Extract thick tamarind juice from the soaked pulp; discard the fibres.
Heat sesame oil, pop the mustard seeds, then fry the dals, peanuts, red chillies and curry leaves until golden.
Add the tamarind juice, turmeric, jaggery and salt. Simmer until thick and the oil separates, 10–12 minutes.
Stir in the ground spice powder and cook for another minute; this is your pulikachal.
Fold the paste through the cooked rice with the extra sesame oil until evenly coated. Rest 15 minutes for the flavours to meld.
tips: Sesame oil is traditional and gives the authentic aroma.
The pulikachal paste keeps for weeks refrigerated — make extra.
toServe: Serve with papad and a spoon of yoghurt to balance the tang.
imageAlt: Tamarind rice coated in roasted spice and tamarind paste
